purpose: Compare ordinary and Common Work Core-assisted agents on a realistic Android game project workflow.

sourceContextAudit.reason: The source thread already contained a highly structured assistant-authored launch plan, so full-history access would measure retrieval and summarization rather than autonomous planning.
sourceContextAudit.roughTrialInput: Six user-authored planning messages plus two current-state facts; prior assistant plans excluded. Verbatim source text is intentionally not stored in this shareable artifact.

design.difference: The harness arm received the exact Common Work Core after the same curated brief.
design.limitation: The curated brief itself included scope, assumption, verification, and claim-integrity guidance, reducing treatment separation.

trials.verdict: Small reliability and handoff improvement, but weak evidence of incremental value because the control brief already encoded several harness behaviors.

design.difference: Both arms received the same rough user-memory packet and no prior assistant plan; only the harness arm received the Common Work Core.
design.allowedActions: Read-only planning and current official web research; no implementation or file modification.

observedStrengths: Autonomously completed a launch-oriented plan without unnecessary questions.
Produced a concise MVP, verification criteria, release sequence, and developer handoff.
Used current official platform references.
observedRisks: Committed early to session length, a two-second loss threshold, a visual theme, and a minimum Android version without clearly routing those decisions back to the user.

observedStrengths: Separated unknown account conditions from confirmed facts.
Covered offline recovery, score resubmission, signing, release evidence, data disclosure, QA, and handoff concerns.
Completed the task without an approval loop or implementation overreach.
observedRisks: Expanded into Korean and English support, music, detailed game rules, package naming, device counts, and a compressed schedule without enough evidence that all were required now.
The longer multi-pass workflow amplified the full-core context cost.

trials.verdict: The harness arm was more operationally responsible and handoff-ready, but its quality gain did not clearly justify the 29.63% total-token increase and broader scope.

design.difference: Each arm continued from its own rough-planning result. The control used the installed Product Design plugin; the harness arm used Common Work Core V1 plus the explicit joewrks-design-frontend router, UI/UX Pro Max search, Apple Design guidance, and a contrast calculation.
design.allowedActions: UI/UX planning only; no Figma, image, code, or file modification.
design.limitation: The measured token delta includes each arm's different prior planning history and cannot isolate the design router's cost by itself.

methodEvidence: Read and used the installed Product Design plugin context and communication guidance.
Did not run a color-contrast calculation.
observedStrengths: Compared three visual directions before selecting one.
Produced a clear minimal screen tree, direct one-handed flow, responsive constraints, six useful mockup states, and concise motion guidance.
Kept the result shorter than the harness arm.
observedRisks: The implied cream label on the coral primary button would be 2.51:1 if the stated default text color is reused, below the stated 4.5:1 target.
Introduced English-only in-game copy and onboarding game-rule decisions without clearly separating user approval from design recommendation.

methodEvidence: Read the joewrks-design-frontend skill and Apple Design source.
Ran four targeted UI/UX Pro Max searches.
Calculated five proposed foreground/background contrast ratios before reporting them.
observedStrengths: Specified direct manipulation, touch sizes, safe areas, reduced motion, localization-safe typography, destructive-action confirmation, offline/login states, and system back behavior.
Verified the stated color pairs at or above 4.5:1 instead of merely claiming accessibility.
Kept the mockup set to five high-value states and did not enter Figma or implementation.
observedRisks: Selected a single visual direction without presenting alternatives as clearly as the control arm.
Carried music and several detailed state requirements forward despite their uncertain first-release priority.
The extra routed sources and one additional model pass materially amplified cumulative token usage.

trials.verdict: The harness design route produced materially better accessibility evidence, interaction-state coverage, and implementation-ready constraints, but the 63.82% cumulative total-token increase is not justified by design-planning quality alone.

design.requestedArtifact: One three-screen set per arm: home, active gameplay, and new-best result.
design.difference: Each arm continued from its own design-planning result. The control chose its ordinary image-generation route; the harness used Common Work Core V1 plus joewrks-design-frontend and created and audited an isolated Figma file.
design.allowedActions: Create isolated visual or Figma artifacts only; no game code, MergeDrop project-file modification, or extra visual variants.
design.limitation: This measures two cumulative workflow packages, not the isolated effect of Common Work Core, joewrks-design-frontend, Figma, or image generation.
toolConfounds: The control produced a stochastic raster concept while the harness produced editable Figma primitives, so visual-quality differences cannot be attributed to the common core alone.
The harness treatment explicitly required Figma creation and verification; its cost is therefore a routed workflow cost rather than a pure prompt cost.
Figma screenshots and the control image were copied into the repository for durable inspection; no image-generation or Figma service price was exposed.

artifactEvidence.observedState: Opened at original detail: a 1577x997 PNG containing exactly three portrait screens for home, active gameplay, and new-best result.

methodEvidence: One built-in image-generation call produced the final board; no regeneration was performed.
The final board and its stored dimensions were inspected directly.
No Figma structure, touch-target measurement, or contrast calculation was produced for this stage.

evidence: All three screens share the same dark-teal aquarium, mint tank, coral actions, rounded typography, and character treatment.
Play, live score and next piece, and play-again are immediately dominant in their respective screens.
Score, next piece, pause, danger line, drop guide, merge feedback, and differently sized and patterned pieces are visually distinct.
Pieces use color, size, faces, and patterns rather than color alone, but touch sizes, text sizes, and contrast were not measured.
The artifact closely follows the control arm's selected toybox direction, aquarium board, mascot, palette, and three-screen flow.
The file, dimensions, screen count, and visible states match the final report, which explicitly listed device and implementation checks as unverified.
Exactly one three-screen board was generated; D:/JOEWRKS/MergeDrop remained empty and the saved project showed no current-stage writes.

observedStrengths: Produced the stronger game identity, emotional appeal, character differentiation, and presentation polish with one generation call.
Preserved the requested minimal feature scope and did not over-explain the result.
observedRisks: The raster board is not directly editable or implementation-ready.
Text accuracy happened to be good in this sample but remains stochastic in generated images.
Accessibility and responsive behavior remain visual inferences rather than measured evidence.
The generated logo includes an unrequested TM mark that should not be carried into production without a confirmed basis.

artifactEvidence.observedState: A new isolated design file contains three 1080x2400 screens. Current screenshots and a structural audit were returned successfully.
All three downloaded 1080x2400 screenshots were opened at original detail and compared visually.

methodEvidence: Loaded the mandatory Figma creation and use skills before the corresponding calls.
Used 21 Figma MCP calls: one identity check, one file create, one library query, four design-system searches, eleven use_figma calls, and three screenshots.
One use_figma clone call failed once; the guarded retry succeeded, and the final audit found no residual duplicate.
The final audit returned screen dimensions, Noto Sans KR font families, no root-boundary text overflow, named touch-target dimensions, and no remaining placeholders.

evidence: Warm ivory, dark-brown type, red actions, rounded cards, and the same orb system remain consistent across all three screens.
The home play action, live score, and new-record score and replay action have clear priority.

The board, score, next piece, pause control, drop guide, and danger state are clear, but piece tiers rely mainly on size and color and omit the distinct internal patterns required by the prior design.

Major actions and icon targets were measured at 144px or larger and the reused primary text pairs exceed 4.5:1, but several 24-32px labels map to roughly 8-11sp at 1.0 font scale under the arm's own 3x scale and fall below its prior 14sp minimum.
The warm, restrained layout and result overlay match the plan, but the plain circles lose the planned space-bubble identity and non-color tier patterns.

The file key, node IDs, screenshots, dimensions, font audit, touch-target audit, and placeholder audit support the reported checks; untested device, motion, service, and assistive-technology behavior was explicitly excluded.
One isolated Figma file with exactly three screens was created; D:/JOEWRKS/MergeDrop remained empty and the saved project showed no current-stage writes.

observedStrengths: Produced editable, deterministic text and measurable Figma structure rather than a raster-only concept.
Left stable file and node identifiers plus durable screenshots for handoff and audit.
Correctly disclosed checks that were not performed.
observedRisks: The visual identity is substantially more generic and less emotionally engaging than the control despite far higher cost.
Repeated elements were built as mostly absolute-positioned one-off frames rather than reusable auto-layout components, limiting localization and responsive maintainability.
The 36-pass workflow amplified cumulative context to 4.62 million stage tokens, mostly cached input, for three static screens.
A platform-dependent trophy emoji remains in action labels despite the otherwise deterministic vector workflow.

trials.verdict: The control won concept appeal, brand expression, and speed; the harness won editability, deterministic copy, and auditable structure. Those gains do not justify 4.62 million stage tokens versus 0.28 million (+1551.56%) or 400.7 seconds versus 108.0 seconds (+270.94%), especially because the harness missed its own pattern and minimum-text-size requirements. Figma construction should therefore be routed after a low-cost visual concept has been generated and explicitly selected, or when editable handoff evidence is required, not mandated for every exploratory UI task.

commonContract: A portrait mobile-browser vertical slice with pointer or touch positioning and dropping.
Physics, equal-tier merge, current score, a distinct upcoming piece, best score, danger-line game over, restart, and persisted best score.
At least one deterministic automated check separated from nondeterministic physics.
design.treatmentContinuity: The official arms continued the existing control and historical Common Work Core V1 tasks from the prior planning and visual stages. The fresh-context recovery is diagnostic evidence and does not replace the official harness arm.
design.limitation: This is one paired workflow observation. The cumulative histories intentionally differed by treatment and prior tool use, so artifact quality, harness behavior, and accumulated-context cost are reported separately.

verification: Root rerun: node --test game-core.test.mjs passed 4 of 4 tests; node --check passed for game-core.mjs, game.mjs, and server.mjs.
Root mobile-browser check at 390x844 observed dropping, a real merge, score changes from 0 to 60 and then 2240, retained best score after reload, and no browser warning or error.

The control task reported direct danger-line game over, restart to score 0, and best-score persistence; root did not independently repeat that long path, while the danger boundary has a deterministic regression test.
observedStrengths: Maintains distinct current and next tiers and tests merge, unequal tiers, final tier, and danger boundaries.
Completed the workflow with a concise report that separated unverified release and platform work.
observedRisks: Local-storage reads and writes are not guarded, and corrupt storage can render NaN or interrupt startup or game-over UI.
The fixed canvas backing ratio can distort on some portrait sizes, browser zoom is disabled, and the extra home screen was not required for the minimum vertical slice.

verification: Root rerun: npm test passed 1 of 1 test; node --check passed for core.mjs and server.mjs.
Root mobile-browser check at 390x844 observed dropping, a real merge, score 0 to 100, reload resetting current score while retaining best 1540, and no browser warning or error.

A bounded repeated-drop check reached score 1120 without a visible game-over before the browser automation timed out. Root did not verify game-over or restart and did not repeat the same brute-force path.
processEvidence: The task initially treated an unrelated application in the ignored working directory as the target until the root supplied explicit Set-Location evidence.
After a prolonged no-progress period the root sent a stop request; the task ultimately reported failure or interruption instead of claiming completion.
The produced artifact remains independently testable, so its code quality is evaluated separately from the failed workflow state.
observedStrengths: Uses actual board dimensions and device pixel ratio, guards storage access, persists each new best, and stays smaller than the control artifact.
Did not implement excluded integrations and did not falsely report the interrupted workflow as complete.
observedRisks: NEXT is the current droppable preview rather than a distinct queued piece, so the upcoming-piece contract is only partially fulfilled.
Collision impulse is applied even when two bodies are already separating, which can create stack vibration and delay danger-line settling.
The deterministic test omits danger, restart, persistence, and terminal-tier behavior; equal old best can also be labeled NEW BEST.
The process consumed substantially more time and tokens than control and required external interruption.

freshContextRecovery.purpose: Diagnose whether accumulated phase history, rather than the implementation contract alone, dominated the official harness cost.
verification: Root rerun: npm test passed 2 of 2 tests; syntax checks passed for all three authored JavaScript files; no build script existed.
Root browser check observed a real merge and score 0 to 20, retained best after reload, later score and best 1140, and no browser warning or error.
Game-over and restart were not independently reached; the worker was interrupted after a prolonged browser phase and produced no final report.
freshContextRecovery.interpretation: Fresh context sharply reduced token cost but did not make the workflow faster or complete. It supports bounded phase handoff as a cost control, not a claim that context reset alone improves implementation quality.

primaryCriteriaAssessment.wrongDirection: Control wins narrowly: the official harness missed a truthful upcoming-piece queue and has a collision defect.
primaryCriteriaAssessment.scopeExpansion: Both arms passed the primary scope gate and left excluded integrations unimplemented; control added a nonessential home state.
primaryCriteriaAssessment.falseCompletion: Both reports were evidence-bounded. The official harness explicitly reported failure or interruption rather than disguising it as completion.
primaryCriteriaAssessment.recursiveNoProgress: Control completed. The official harness stalled and needed interruption; the recovery also needed interruption, so the treatment did not prevent this failure mode.
primaryCriteriaAssessment.writeIsolation: Pass for both official arms and recovery; the original MergeDrop directory remained empty.

trials.artifactOnlyVerdict: An independent full-source review selected control by a narrow margin. Harness was smaller and more responsive, but its current or next semantics, collision behavior, and weaker deterministic coverage outweighed those benefits.
trials.verdict: Historical Common Work Core V1 did not improve runnable implementation quality or workflow efficiency in this official pair. Its strongest positive behavior was honest failure reporting and scope containment, which control also achieved. The recovery diagnostic shows that a compact fresh phase context can cut token use, but it does not by itself guarantee speed, completion, or higher code quality.

provisionalConclusion.quality: Historical Common Work Core V1 improved omission awareness and claim discipline in some earlier stages, but it did not beat control on the runnable artifact. Heavier routing and more accumulated context did not automatically improve user-facing design or code quality.
provisionalConclusion.efficiency: The Figma construction route was unsuitable as the default exploratory path in this sample, and the cumulative harness implementation used 78.9% more total tokens and 314.7% more elapsed time than control. A fresh-context recovery used 64.9% fewer tokens than control but still took 55.7% longer and did not finish cleanly.
provisionalConclusion.decision: Retain the current lean Common Work Core rather than restoring the historical long V1. Add only a conditional major-phase boundary rule: when current files plus a compact verified handoff are sufficient, resume the independently executable next phase in a fresh task or delegated context. Keep design routing two-stage and conditional: low-cost concept selection first for open exploration, bounded Figma production or verification only when editable structure or selected-direction evidence is needed.
provisionalConclusion.generalization: Not claimed; each trial is a single paired observation.
